raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through. It's spring, and I need to lay out the year.

---

**My reasoning (as the farmer):**

I've been working this land for 55 years. At my age, I keep things close to what I know works. My 10.1 mu breaks into roughly 6 mu of chili — that's my cash crop, the one that pays for everything — and 4.1 mu on the wheat-maize rotation for our own grain and some to sell.

The chili is the main thing. I'll plant Hebei hybrid line (辣丰 type), transplant seedlings around late April after the soil warms. Chili is a heavy feeder and my yield expectation is around 300 kg dry/mu — I budget about 22 kg N/mu total, split: 12 kg base with compost and compound fertilizer before ridging, then two topdressings at flowering and early fruiting. P and K matter more than people realize for fruit set, so I'll put in about 8 kg P2O5 and 12 kg K2O/mu with the base. Chili needs water — I'll irrigate 4-5 times from transplanting through pod fill. Pesticide is unavoidable: anthracnose and aphids every year, so I spray preventively. The harvest is where my labor problem shows up — me, my wife, and one son can't pick 6 mu of chili, so I'll hire 15-20 day-laborers through September-October.

The winter wheat I planted last October is already up and I'll topdress urea at jointing, around 8-10 kg N/mu, and irrigate at jointing and again at grain-filling. I expect around 450 kg/mu — the field has good history. After harvest in early June, I turn straight around for summer maize — no tillage, just no-till seeding with a Zhengdan 958 hybrid within 3-4 days. Maize gets about 15 kg N/mu, mostly at V6 big-bell stage, and I'll irrigate once at tasseling if June-July is dry. Yield target around 500 kg/mu.

Total input budget is tight — chili alone eats most of it. I calculate I'll spend around 9,500 yuan on inputs, not counting hired labor. That leaves us thin on cash until the chili sells in October, but I've run this system for years and I know the rhythm.
